nl-15kd.title: Lamp post: horizontal white sticker, 1-2 digits
nl-15kd.summary: The southern province next to it also has white stickers on street lights, but horizontal with only one or two digits.

nl-36OP.title: Roadside: brick rumble strip
nl-36OP.summary: Many country roads have a strip of bricks along the edge, almost unique and useful on very rural roads.

nl-58qC.title: Google car: black back showing through blur
nl-58qC.summary: In some Gen 4 coverage a glitch in the blur shows the black back of the Google car.

nl-5Rdh.title: Landscape: marshy polder, many small waterways
nl-5Rdh.summary: The west and north are at or below sea level, with marshy 'polder' countryside full of small waterways.

nl-8MuM.title: Landscape: waterways, canals, dikes
nl-8MuM.summary: Countless waterways. Canals and ditches beside the road are common, along with dikes (low earth walls), dams and bridges.

nl-9wTg.title: Street sign: neighbourhood name plus number
nl-9wTg.summary: Many streets in Lelystad are named after their neighbourhood followed by a number. Some of these names show on the map.

nl-ABWw.title: Street sign: district in small text below name
nl-ABWw.summary: The capital's street signs show the city district in smaller letters under the street name. Very uncommon elsewhere.

nl-ANbj.title: Landscape: greenhouses everywhere
nl-ANbj.summary: Greenhouses cover most of the land in one municipality southwest of The Hague.

nl-Awqc.title: Language: double vowels, ij, ieuw, oe
nl-Awqc.summary: A Germanic language with lots of double vowels and clusters like ij, ieuw and oe. A single capital IJ is unique to it. Also spoken in northern Belgium.

nl-B3Dg.title: Sign: blue direction signs, white bike signs
nl-B3Dg.summary: Direction signs are blue with white text. Signs for cyclists are white with a red border.

nl-BWFN.title: Landscape: extremely flat, below sea level
nl-BWFN.summary: Extremely flat, with only a few metres of height difference in most places. Large areas are reclaimed land at or below sea level. Low hills exist in the far south and in a central forest area.

nl-CVMV.title: Houses: row houses everywhere
nl-CVMV.summary: Almost half of all homes are row houses, far more than in most European countries.

nl-ChWn.title: Sign: striped signposts, black-white or blue-white
nl-ChWn.summary: Many signposts have stripes in black and white or blue and white.

nl-Cw0P.title: Sign: edge border visible from behind
nl-Cw0P.summary: Road sign edges wrap around to the back, giving a border visible from behind, sometimes in the sign's colour. Consistent and unique.

nl-FPtB.title: Landscape: forest, heath and sandy soil
nl-FPtB.summary: An unusually forested central area with slight elevation, old forest, heath or sandy soil. It can look odd compared with the rest of the country. Other natural areas can look similar, but this is the biggest.

nl-FqgZ.title: Street sign: yellow text on red
nl-FqgZ.summary: One municipality near Leiden uses hard-to-read street signs with yellow text on a red background.

nl-HYcL.title: Sidewalk: square grey tiles, offset pattern
nl-HYcL.summary: Most sidewalks use square grey tiles laid in an offset pattern. Some old areas have small brick sidewalks.

nl-Hj6A.title: Roads: rows of trees along rural roads
nl-Hj6A.summary: Many country roads are lined with rows of trees. Common in Poland too.

nl-HxdF.title: Route marker: green with A or N number
nl-HxdF.summary: Green road markers with the number in a small box. Motorways have a red box and start with A, regional roads a yellow box and N. Some have province-specific designs.

nl-IMIN.title: Flags: provincial flags, two common ones
nl-IMIN.summary: Every province has its own flag, but most are rarely seen. The Friesland and Noord-Brabant flags are common, and an unofficial flag of the Achterhoek region in the east is popular.

nl-IYay.title: Landmark: huge harbour with round fuel tanks
nl-IYay.summary: The Rotterdam harbour runs from downtown to the coast. Heavy industry and large round fuel tanks suggest it. Amsterdam and Delfzijl harbours also have fuel tanks.

nl-Jaik.title: Language: ^ vowels, wei or strjitte endings
nl-Jaik.summary: In the northern province, Frisian is spoken, so many town signs show two names. Some streets end in -wei or -strjitte. Frisian has letters Â, Ê, Ô, Û and uses Y a lot more than Dutch.

nl-JnCa.title: Roadside: bike paths, often reddish-pink
nl-JnCa.summary: Many roads have bicycle paths beside them, often a reddish-pink lane. Cyclists are everywhere.

nl-KAD1.title: Landscape: low hills in the far south
nl-KAD1.summary: Southern Limburg has some low hills, unlike the rest of the very flat country.

nl-KgeR.title: Towns: very organised, planned suburbs
nl-KgeR.summary: A tidy, planned look with well-kept roads. Suburbs are master-planned and usually made of row houses.

nl-KiZn.title: Coverage: trekker with brown hair visible
nl-KiZn.summary: In a national park in the central forest area, a trekker shows the brown hair of the Google employee.

nl-NyGc.title: Landmark: windmills and wind turbines
nl-NyGc.summary: Both traditional water or grain windmills and modern wind turbines are common.

nl-OL78.title: Coast: lined with dunes
nl-OL78.summary: Most of the North Sea coast is lined by sand dunes.

nl-PKNI.title: Route marker: regional designs and km stickers
nl-PKNI.summary: Regional N-road markers (yellow box) sometimes have province-specific designs, others are generic. Motorway markers (red box) are all the same. Bollards may carry region-specific km stickers.

nl-PQs0.title: Location: Caribbean island north of Venezuela
nl-PQs0.summary: A Caribbean country in the Kingdom, north of western Venezuela. It counts as the Netherlands for streaks.

differs.how: Caribbean island with its own guide

nl-R6It.title: Bollard: plain white, red reflector
nl-R6It.summary: A simple white bollard with a red reflector. Rarely, round French-style bollards appear, but their red band usually doesn't wrap fully around.

differs.how: French red band goes all the way around

nl-SU02.title: Plate: long yellow with blue strip
nl-SU02.summary: Long yellow plates with the blue European strip on the left. Taxis have blue plates. Yellow plates also exist in Luxembourg and the UK (rear only), and on Danish commercial vehicles.

differs.how: only rear plates are yellow, often no blue strip

nl-SWmB.title: Houses: rolling shutters in the south
nl-SWmB.summary: Roll-down window shutters are more common in the southern half, but exist in the north too, so use with caution.

nl-TIzw.title: Coverage: northwest islands with dunes
nl-TIzw.summary: The Wadden Islands in the northwest are popular tourist spots, which sometimes shows in the coverage. Their northwest coasts have lots of dunes.

nl-TXoh.title: Landscape: man-made, ruler-straight roads, big fields
nl-TXoh.summary: A province reclaimed from the sea in the mid 20th century: extremely straight roads, big crop fields, wind turbines and no historic buildings. The one exception is Urk, on a former island.

nl-ZZh6.title: Houses: farms with very large roofs
nl-ZZh6.summary: Farms in the north often have very large roofs.

nl-bLrf.title: Road: brick paving
nl-bLrf.summary: Brick roads are common in towns and countryside, often in one particular pattern.

nl-dIs0.title: Guardrail: striped barrier
nl-dIs0.summary: Distinctive striped barriers on some roads, especially in the countryside.

nl-eSJE.title: Street sign: blue with white text, straat
nl-eSJE.summary: Street signs are almost always blue with white text. Rarely yellow, white or green. Names end in straat, -weg, -laan, -pad, -plein. 'Fietspad' just means bike path. Belgium's signs vary in colour and name the municipality.

differs.how: signs vary in colour and show the municipality

nl-hcMa.title: Phone numbers: 3-4 digit area codes, mobile 06
nl-hcMa.summary: Landlines start with a 3 or 4 digit area code, grouped by region (except 07 and two 02 codes). Mobiles start with 06, which no landline code uses.

nl-kG3k.title: Houses: green or black wood with white trim
nl-kG3k.summary: North of the capital, buildings often have wooden parts painted green or black with white trim, and sometimes tall white roof spires.

nl-keUQ.title: Landscape: typical flat farmland
nl-keUQ.summary: The south and east look like ordinary flat European farmland. Waterways exist but the land is less marshy.

nl-lZws.title: Google car: low-mounted camera, big round blur
nl-lZws.summary: A Gen 4 camera mounted lower than normal, with a fairly large round blur and a small bump at the front. The blur can be see-through. Most of Western Europe has it.

nl-lm-2998.title: Sign: pedestrian figure with starfish limbs
nl-lm-2998.summary: The figure has funny limbs that shrink toward the end, like a starfish.

nl-lm-740399.title: Houses: many tall skyscrapers
nl-lm-740399.summary: If you know you are in the country and see many tall buildings, it is most likely Rotterdam, which has most of the skyscrapers. The Hague and Amsterdam have some too.

nl-nqei.title: Sign: blue town entry with municipality
nl-nqei.summary: Blue town entry signs, sometimes elaborate with frames and extra signs. They often show the municipality after 'gemeente' (gem), which is often named after a nearby bigger town.

nl-oG0B.title: Border: Belgian enclaves in town
nl-oG0B.summary: A southern town contains Belgian enclaves, shown by pavement markings and Dutch and Belgian flags flown together.

nl-qfv9.title: Road: straight dam with water on one side
nl-qfv9.summary: A long straight divided highway on a dam running southwest to northeast, with water to the southeast and a dike to the northwest. Other big dams exist but this is the biggest.

nl-qzbi.title: Pole: no street-level utility poles
nl-qzbi.summary: Almost no small utility poles, only big power lines. Belgium uses utility poles fairly often.

nl-r0hh.title: Lamp post: tall white sticker, 3-4 digits
nl-r0hh.summary: A long vertical white sticker with three or four digits on street lights is found in the far south-east.

nl-vamQ.title: Houses: red-brown brick, orange or grey tiles
nl-vamQ.summary: Brick buildings are very common, mostly red-brown, with orange or dark grey roof tiles. Denmark and Belgium look similar.

nl-xEO9.title: Sign: bulky yellow signpost on islands
nl-xEO9.summary: Road signs on traffic islands often sit on bulky yellow posts.

nl-xQ7P.title: Speed bump: long and short white stripes
nl-xQ7P.summary: Speed bumps with white warning stripes alternating long and short, on brick and on asphalt.

nl-ymqD.title: Road lines: all white, dashed edge lines
nl-ymqD.summary: All white lines, as in most of Europe, and many roads have dashed edge lines. Occasionally green centre lines appear.
